technical.summary: Short-term momentum is bullish with RSI and moving average confluence, but intermediate trend weakness (below 50-MA, negative ADX, weak money flow) and overbought stochRSI limit swing entry probability.

fundamental.summary: YUM shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signal, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and elevated earnings risk within 47 days.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (19/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but congressional activity is neutral with mixed trades from junior member 106+ days ago; no recent news sentiment available to confirm setup.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (317), strong dollar pressures multinational YUM, and earnings in 47 days add event risk.

debate.key_bull_argument: Short-term RSI/SMA confluence and supertrend bullish signal with price near support (106.89) offer tactical entry for swing traders in extreme fear environment.
debate.key_bear_argument: Intermediate trend collapse (below 50-MA, negative ADX, weak money flow), stochRSI overbought, macro crisis (inverted yield curve, VIX 317, strong dollar), zero fundamental conviction, and earnings event risk in 47 days overwhelm short-term technicals.

decision.entry_rationale: Short-term technicals (RSI, SMA confluence, supertrend) offer tactical setup at support, and extreme fear sentiment presents contrarian opportunity. However, intermediate trend collapse, macro crisis conditions, zero fundamental conviction, and imminent earnings event (47 days) create asymmetric downside risk that outweighs swing entry merit.
decision.primary_risk: Inverted yield curve + VIX crisis + strong dollar headwinds create macro environment hostile to discretionary consumer stocks; earnings in 47 days adds binary event risk that can gap through technical support.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case; technical bull case insufficient to overcome fundamental, sentiment, and macro consensus
